lines.speaker: Croesus
lines.text: We can't stand it, Pluto—this dog Menippus living right next door. Move him, or we move.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: What harm does he do you? He's dead, same as you.
lines.description: weary administrator, dry and mildly puzzled

lines.speaker: Croesus
lines.text: Whenever we start wailing and moaning about the old days—Midas here about his gold, Sardanapalus about all that luxury, me about my treasures—he laughs at us. Calls us slaves and scum. Sometimes he even sings over us and ruins the whole lament. He's a complete pest.
lines.description: aggrieved testimony, building a ridiculous legal case

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: Menippus. What do you say to that?
lines.description: formal docket tone, tired but fair

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: It's true, Pluto. I despise them. Base, rotten types. Living badly wasn't enough for them—now they're dead badly too, still clinging to the world above. So yes, I enjoy annoying them.
lines.description: cheerfully candid, delighted rather than defensive

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: You shouldn't. They're grieving real losses.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: You're being ridiculous, Pluto, siding with their groans.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: I'm not siding with anyone. I just don't want fighting in my jurisdiction.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Well then, you dregs of Lydia, Phrygia, and Assyria—get this straight: I am not stopping. Wherever you go, I'll follow, needling you, singing over you, laughing at you.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: No. The outrage was what you did—demanding worship, lording it over free men, never once thinking about death. So now you can wail, stripped of everything.
lines.description: dry correction, moral point without sermonizing

lines.speaker: Croesus
lines.text: So many great possessions, by the gods.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: That's the spirit. You keep moaning, and I'll sing “Know thyself” over and over. It suits this kind of performance.
lines.description: pleased deadpan, landing the final needle
